caption: The drawing, rendered in black pencil or ink on a light beige background, features two primary views of a desk along with labeled components. On the left side, there is an elevation (front) view showing a desk with a tall upper cabinet topped with an urn-shaped finial. Beneath the cabinet are open arcaded shelves, with a solid door on the left portion marked “BOOK CASE,” and three open spaces labeled “SPACE” and “SHELF” below the writing surface. To the right of this elevation is a plan (top) view labeled as “WRITING SURFACE OF DESK,” indicating a central area covered in “VELVET,” bordered by a wood frame and additional detailed notes. Below the writing surface plan is a partial leg detail, showing linear features and fluting along the leg, with further notes indicating textures and materials. Several labels clarify which parts of the desk are drawers or pull-outs, and the text also notes the Metropolitan Museum of Art as a reference location. All lines are thin, precise, and technical, without shading or color fill, and the overall composition is arranged with significant blank space around the drawing for clarity.
title: Desk
